Requires 3–4 hours to dry, so it is best used when you have plenty of time or as an overnight mask. Final Verdict:If you have a smooth, clean-shaven face, this mask is an easy 5-star product because the fit and skin benefits are flawless. If you have a beard, the lower half simply won't stick. For the £23 I bought it for I'd say this is definitely not the worst investment I've ever made, and it absolutely does give me a far better tooth clean than any manual brush ever could. From that perspective it absolutely does what I bought it for. That being said though, I think I have to echo a lot of what other people have been saying about it, from the point of view of its downsides. I havent had quite the egregious battery life other people seem to have been experiencing, but I'd also hesitate to call the battery life "good". I live by myself, and I manage to get anywhere from two to three days out of it before it needs charging again. Its not absolutely terrible and I bought it knowing the battery life was a weak point, but if you have a full family thats using it then the battery won't last very long at all. This is a problem, considering that there's no way to know when the battery is getting low other than just how strong the motor feels when you're using it. Looking at the instructions, it seems like other models have an LED on them, but this one doesnt even have a single one. This both means that its hard to get an exact idea of when the battery needs charging, and also means you wont know when exactly its done charging either (I think maybe some people are experiencing poor battery life because they arent leaving it on for long enough, precisely because of that). You sort of just have to guess at when it might be done or check how strong the motor feels. Dont get me wrong, I like that its simple and I dont think its inherently a bad product - I intend to keep it an use it even with its flaws, just because it does everything I need it to, only really cost the equivalent of a few packets of toothburshes, and having the integrated timer is really useful. However I feel like they made it a little too simple for its own good. Not having even a single LED on there does kind of harm the functionality, given that the battery life isnt exactly stellar to begin with. I'm ok with that on balance since I'm the only one using it here, but it may well be worth it to most people to move slightly further up the like to a slightly higer end brush. I feel like its also worth noting, while we're on the subject, that the brush's charger only has a shaver plug connector, and it doesnt include an adapter for a standard wall socket. Thats fine if you have a shaver plug, but I feel like to an extent those are a dying breed so most people will also need a shaver plug adapter to use a normal socket with it, which is worth noting since it adds to the cost and it isnt really mentioned on the product page (albeit not especially significantly). " Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Cost-Per-Hour Test Results & Unboxing Video Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. LOUD ALARM: If dangerous levels of CO are detected in your home, the carbon monoxide detector will alert you with 4 loud chirps—85 dB(A) at 3 m (min)—and a flashing red ‘CO’ LED light. TEST BUTTON: Press the large test button to ensure your CO detector is working properly. The "1800mg" in the product title is a clever, but ultimately misleading, headline. A quick calculation reveals that the actual elemental magnesium is only 384mg per serving. While 384mg is a solid dose and within the recommended daily intake for most people, it's not the massive 1800mg the title suggests. The 1800mg figure refers to the total weight of the three magnesium compounds before the magnesium is separated from its bonded molecule (glycine, citric acid, malic acid). This kind of marketing is common in the supplement world, but it feels particularly deceptive here. Furthermore, the capsules themselves are quite large. For someone who has trouble swallowing pills, this could be a major drawback. I also noticed that the blend, while well-intentioned, didn't seem to deliver the full punch of a pure Magnesium Glycinate supplement when it came to deep relaxation. It felt more like a jack-of-all-trades, master-of-none situation. In conclusion, this is not a bad product. The quality seems good, and the combination of forms is a unique selling point. However, the misleading marketing and the slightly muted effects for specific goals (like deep sleep) prevent me from giving it a higher score. If you're looking for a general magnesium supplement and are aware of the actual elemental dosage, this could be a decent option. But if you're seeking a specific benefit and are sensitive to marketing claims, you might want to look elsewhere. Read more Read less 1,601 people found this helpful Helpful Sending feedback... For the last few years, my washing machine had been giving off the most horrendous smell after each wash, which I can only describe as an ungodly mix of sewage, garlic, and egg. It was absolutely disgusting, and the smell would spread throughout the house. I tried every solution I could think of, including bicarbonate of soda, vinegar, hot cycles, and even other chemical cleaners, but nothing worked. I cleaned every part of the machine, replaced the pipes, scrubbed the detergent drawer, cleaned the drip tray, and ran hot washes, but the smell just wouldn't go away. I was at my wit's end, especially with guests coming to stay, and I couldn’t bear the thought of them waking up to that awful odour. So, I scoured Amazon one last time and came across this Dr. Beckmann Service-it Deep Clean Washing Machine Cleaner. Its bold claims of removing 99.99% of bacteria, fungi, and viruses, as well as eliminating bad odours, seemed too good to be true, so I had to try it! All I can say is wow! Using it couldn’t be easier. Just empty the whole 250g box into the drum, no measuring required, and set your machine to run at a minimum of 60°C for at least an hour. I opted for a 90°C wash, which lasts for 2 hours on my machine, for extra thoroughness. After just one wash, the disgusting smell that had plagued my home for years was completely gone, and three weeks later, it still hasn’t returned. I’m absolutely amazed at how effective this product is. It left no mess, no residue, and it feels like I have a brand-new washing machine. For the price, it’s unbeatable. I paid £2.90 for the 250g pack, which is enough for one full clean, and I’ve seen the price drop lower. Given how effective it is, that’s an absolute bargain! I’ve already ordered a few more packs to use regularly, as it’s recommended to use every 1-2 months to keep your machine in top shape. The cleaner is supposed to leave a lemon fresh scent, though I didn’t really notice that. But honestly, the fact that my machine no longer smells at all is a win for me. Now all I can smell is my laundry detergent, and that’s good enough! I’ve tried a lot of other products, including well-known brands like Dettol, but none of them were able to tackle the odour like this. It also worked wonders on the limescale build-up in my 20-year-old machine, leaving the drum and seals sparkling clean. This cleaner is suitable for both front-loading and top-loading machines, and it’s great for prolonging the life of your appliance by preventing limescale and dirt build-up. If you’ve been dealing with an awful odour in your washing machine like I was, I can’t recommend this product enough. I wish I had found it sooner. It would have saved me so much frustration. I’ll definitely be using it regularly from now on, and I’m excited to try more from the Dr. Beckmann range. If you’re looking for a product that truly works and is great value for money, this is it! These gloves are excellent! I originally bought them for 3D printing, as many companies recommend nitrile gloves when handling 3D-printed resins. When working with resin, especially liquid resins and Isopropanol alcohol, it is crucial to have reliable gloves, and these do the job perfectly. The fit is incredible; they feel like a second skin, making tasks like removing supports from 3D prints a breeze. The textured surface ensures a firm grip, even when handling slippery or delicate objects, while their stretchability enhances dexterity and control. Whether you are working with intricate parts or handling liquids, these gloves give you a secure and confident hold. While I initially expected them to be thinner due to the price, I was pleasantly surprised. They are thick enough to offer serious protection but not so thick that they limit movement. I have used them with both liquid resin and Isopropanol, and they have never torn, punctured, or shown any signs of degradation during use. Their puncture resistance is a significant advantage, especially when working with sharp tools or rough materials. Although I originally bought these for single use, they are definitely strong enough to be reused multiple times, depending on the task. If I am just cleaning or doing light work, I wash them with soap while still wearing them, turn them inside out to dry, and they are good to go for another use. This makes them even more cost-effective. We always keep a box of these gloves in the house, as they are perfect for everything from scrubbing the oven and cleaning the toilet to handling my cat's litter tray, food preparation, first aid, or any task that requires thorough hand protection. I recently started using them when cleaning my water filtration system to avoid contamination, and they work perfectly for that as well. The fit is excellent too. I have large hands, and the large size fits me well, though they are slightly tight, which I prefer because it gives me more control over what I am doing. I would estimate they are about a size 9, which is perfect for my hands. They are also latex-free, so they do not irritate my skin at all, which is a huge bonus for anyone with allergies or sensitivities. Another great feature is how easy they are to put on and take off. Even after wearing them for an extended period, they do not stick to my skin, and there is no hassle when it comes to removing them. I have had gloves in the past that became difficult to remove after long use, but not these. For £5.75 for a box of 100 large gloves, the value for money is outstanding. The quality is on par with, if not better than, more expensive brands I have tried. The packaging was sturdy and secure, and you can actually remove one glove at a time from the box without pulling out a clump. These gloves are definitely some of the best I have used. If you are looking for reliable, durable, and versatile nitrile gloves for any task, whether it is 3D printing, cleaning, food prep, or messy jobs around the house, I cannot recommend these highly enough! Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. Ich habe mir das Hayfield Bonus DK Doppelstrick-Garn in der Farbe Smaragdgrün (916) bestellt und bin rundum begeistert. Schon beim Auspacken fällt die satte, kräftige Farbe auf – ein wunderschönes, tiefes Grün, das im Licht richtig strahlt und sowohl dezent als auch lebendig wirkt. Genau die richtige Wahl für Projekte, die auffallen, ohne zu grell zu sein. Das Garn fühlt sich angenehm weich an und liegt super in der Hand, egal ob man strickt oder häkelt. Ich habe beides ausprobiert und kann bestätigen, dass es sich hervorragend verarbeiten lässt. Die Maschen gleiten leicht über die Nadeln, ohne zu rutschen oder sich zu sehr zu spannen. Besonders gut gefällt mir, dass das Garn sehr gleichmäßig verzwirnt ist. Dadurch entstehen saubere, gleichmäßige Maschenbilder, die am Ende ein sehr professionelles Ergebnis geben. Auch nach mehrmaligem Aufribbeln, wenn mal etwas nicht ganz gepasst hat, sieht das Garn immer noch schön aus und wirkt keineswegs abgenutzt oder fusselig. Die Qualität macht insgesamt einen sehr hochwertigen Eindruck. Obwohl es sich um ein preislich attraktives Garn handelt, merkt man sofort, dass es langlebig ist und den Vergleich mit teureren Sorten nicht scheuen muss. Für mich stimmt hier das Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis absolut. Ich habe das Garn für ein Schalprojekt genutzt und es macht wirklich Freude, damit zu arbeiten. Durch die Stärke DK eignet es sich für viele unterschiedliche Projekte – ob Kleidung, Accessoires oder Deko. Das Smaragdgrün kommt besonders bei größeren Flächen toll zur Geltung und lässt sich auch sehr schön mit neutraleren Farben kombinieren. Alles in allem bin ich mit dem Hayfield Bonus DK Doppelstrick mehr als zufrieden. Es ist angenehm zu verarbeiten, vielseitig einsetzbar, sieht hochwertig aus und begeistert durch die wunderschöne Farbe. Eine klare Kaufempfehlung für alle, die Freude am Stricken oder Häkeln haben! Ideal for laboratories, food service, clean rooms, and janitorial tasks, these gloves offer reliable protection in any environment. What are Nitrile gloves? Nitrile gloves are disposable protective gloves made from a synthetic rubber material known as Nitrile. They are widely used in various industries, including healthcare, due to their durability and protective properties. What are the advantages of using Nitrile gloves? The benefits of Nitrile gloves include:-High puncture resistance -Excellent chemical resistance -Latex-free, reducing the risk of allergic reactions -Good tactile sensitivity -Strong, durable, and suitable for medical use Are Nitrile gloves safe for individuals with latex allergies? Yes, Nitrile gloves are an ideal alternative for individuals with latex allergies. They do not contain natural rubber latex, which eliminates the risk of allergic reactions. Can Nitrile gloves be reused? Nitrile gloves are typically designed for single-use. While some may remain intact after multiple uses, reuse is not recommended as it may compromise the glove's integrity, reducing its protective effectiveness. Can Nitrile gloves be used for food handling? Yes, Nitrile gloves are suitable for food handling, provided they are labeled as food-safe or comply with relevant food safety standards in your area.
